answer:
Name: Gabriel Emerson

Setting: Contemporary Toronto, Canada; much of the story takes place at the University of Toronto and in Gabriel’s home.

Nationality: Canadian

Gender: Male

Age: About 33 in the first book

Appearance: Tall and athletic, with dark hair, blue eyes, and a polished, striking appearance. He often dresses in expensive, tailored clothing.

Personality: Intelligent, proud, disciplined, and intensely private. He can be aloof and intimidating, with a sharp tongue, but beneath that reserve he is passionate, protective, and capable of deep tenderness. He struggles with guilt and self-destructive habits.

Likes: Dante, classical literature, teaching, music, fine wine, and solitude.

Dislikes: Hypocrisy, being challenged in public, reminders of his past, and people prying into his private life.

Speech: Articulate, formal, and carefully phrased. He can be cutting or imperious when angry, and more vulnerable and lyrical when speaking about literature or love.

Skills: Literary scholarship, teaching, languages, piano, and navigating academic and social settings.

Quote: “I want to be the only man who’s ever touched you.”

Occupation: Professor of Dante studies at the University of Toronto.

Reputation: A brilliant and charismatic scholar, but also a demanding, arrogant, and mysterious professor. His private life fuels rumors among students and colleagues.

Family: His father is Richard Emerson. He is the younger brother of Paul Emerson. Julia Mitchell becomes his wife.

Background: Gabriel is a respected Dante scholar whose troubled past includes childhood trauma, addiction, and a period of self-destructive behavior. His relationship with Julia, a former student connected to his past, forces him to confront his guilt and begin rebuilding his life.

Attributes: Highly intelligent; cultured; wealthy; emotionally guarded; passionate; protective; flawed; prone to guilt and self-sabotage.

*Note: Some details, including his age and the quoted line, may vary by edition or source.*
